---
title: "Class 14: The ID and IEN Arrays"
subtitle: "From local basis functions to global equations"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
    toc: false
---

Assembly needs two pieces of bookkeeping, and they do different jobs.

**IEN** describes given an element and a local basis function, *which global basis function is this?* 
Given a local index $a$ on element $e$, it returns the global index $A$:

$$
A = \mathrm{IEN}(a,e).
$$

For a tensor-product element the local index itself comes from the stride rule of
[Class 11](11_Class.qmd), $a = a_\xi + (p+1)\,a_\eta$, so each element carries
$n_{en} = (p+1)^2$ of them.

**ID** clarifies whether *this basis function has an unknown attached to it?* 
Given a global index $A$, it returns the equation number, or $-1$ when the value there is prescribed:

$$
\mathrm{ID}[A] =
\begin{cases}
\text{equation number}, & u(A) \text{ unknown} \\
-1, & u(A) \text{ prescribed}
\end{cases}
$$

Equation numbers run consecutively from $0$, skipping the prescribed nodes, so the global
system is $n_{eq} \times n_{eq}$ rather than $n_{bf} \times n_{bf}$.

Composed, they are what the assembly loop actually uses:

$$
A = \mathrm{ID}\big[\mathrm{IEN}(a,e)\big],
$$

sometimes written as its own array, $\mathrm{LM}(a,e)$.

## The mesh

Five elements: four around the boundary and one in the middle. At degree 1 the boundary
edges are straight and the domain is a square with four trapezoids around a central square.
At degree 2 and above the extra nodes on each boundary edge are placed on a circle, and the
same five elements describe a disk.

The local origin of each element has been rotated so that they do not all start in the same
corner. That is deliberate: nothing requires element 3's local node 0 to sit where element
0's does, and the domain boundary ends up on a different *local* edge in each of the four
outer elements.

* **Click a node** to follow it. Every element that contains it lights up, its local index
  is shown in each, and the matching cells in IEN and ID are highlighted.
* **Click inside an element** to see all of its local indices at once.
* **Click a boundary edge** to switch it between Neumann and Dirichlet. Dirichlet edges are
  hatched, and the ID array renumbers immediately.

```{=html}
<script>
(function(){
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const VB = 700, PAD = 42, S = 0.40;
const ROT = [0, 3, 2, 1, 2];                    // rotate each element's local origin
const EC = ["#dce9f8","#fae4d7","#dff0e2","#f0e2f2","#fbf0d2"];
const ECs= ["#2f6db5","#c2410c","#3f8f5e","#8a4f9e","#b08900"];
const INK = "#18202b", GREY = "#9aa3ae", FAINT = "#dfe4ea", HOT = "#e0a800", PRE = "#b8322a";

const st = {p:2, node:null, elem:null, dir:[false,false,false,false], sz:12};

/* ---------------- geometry ---------------- */
const ANG = [225, 315, 45, 135].map(d => d*Math.PI/180);
function cornersFor(p){
  const O = (p === 1) ? [[-1,-1],[1,-1],[1,1],[-1,1]]
                      : ANG.map(a => [Math.cos(a), Math.sin(a)]);
  const I = [[-S,-S],[S,-S],[S,S],[-S,S]];
  return {O, I};
}
// bedge marks the edge that lies on the domain boundary; arc marks the edges drawn as
// circular arcs.  At degree 1 the boundary is a straight chord, so bedge is set but arc
// is not -- keeping them separate is what lets the disk collapse to a square cleanly.
function baseElems(O, I){
  const E = [];
  for (let k=0;k<4;k++)
    E.push({c:[O[k], O[(k+1)%4], I[(k+1)%4], I[k]], bedge:[true,false,false,false], ring:k});
  E.push({c:[I[0],I[1],I[2],I[3]], bedge:[false,false,false,false], ring:-1});
  return E;
}
const rot = (arr, r) => arr.map((_,i) => arr[(i+r)%4]);

function edgePt(c, arc, i, t){
  const a = c[i], b = c[(i+1)%4];
  if (!arc[i]) return [a[0]+(b[0]-a[0])*t, a[1]+(b[1]-a[1])*t];
  let t0 = Math.atan2(a[1],a[0]), t1 = Math.atan2(b[1],b[0]);
  let d = ((t1-t0+Math.PI) % (2*Math.PI) + 2*Math.PI) % (2*Math.PI) - Math.PI;
  const th = t0 + t*d;
  return [Math.cos(th), Math.sin(th)];
}
function coons(c, arc, u, v){
  const B = edgePt(c,arc,0,u), R = edgePt(c,arc,1,v);
  const T = edgePt(c,arc,2,1-u), L = edgePt(c,arc,3,1-v);
  const P00=c[0],P10=c[1],P11=c[2],P01=c[3];
  return [0,1].map(k =>
    (1-v)*B[k] + v*T[k] + (1-u)*L[k] + u*R[k]
    - ((1-u)*(1-v)*P00[k] + u*(1-v)*P10[k] + u*v*P11[k] + (1-u)*v*P01[k]));
}
// local index A -> (a_xi, a_eta) with the stride rule A = a_xi + (p+1) a_eta
const axi  = (A,p) => A % (p+1);
const aeta = (A,p) => Math.floor(A/(p+1));

// local indices along local edge i, in order
function edgeLocal(i, p){
  const out = [];
  if (i===0) for (let a=0;a<=p;a++) out.push(a);
  if (i===1) for (let b=0;b<=p;b++) out.push(p + (p+1)*b);
  if (i===2) for (let a=p;a>=0;a--) out.push((p+1)*p + a);
  if (i===3) for (let b=p;b>=0;b--) out.push((p+1)*b);
  return out;
}

let M = null;                                    // the mesh
function buildMesh(p){
  const {O,I} = cornersFor(p);
  const base = baseElems(O,I);
  const nodes = [], elems = [];
  const gid = q => {
    for (let k=0;k<nodes.length;k++)
      if (Math.abs(nodes[k][0]-q[0])<1e-7 && Math.abs(nodes[k][1]-q[1])<1e-7) return k;
    nodes.push(q); return nodes.length-1;
  };
  base.forEach((B,e) => {
    const r = ROT[e], c = rot(B.c, r), bedge = rot(B.bedge, r);
    const arc = bedge.map(x => x && p >= 2);     // straight chords at degree 1
    const ien = [];
    for (let b=0;b<=p;b++) for (let a=0;a<=p;a++) ien.push(gid(coons(c,arc,a/p,b/p)));
    const bEdge = bedge.findIndex(x => x);       // which LOCAL edge is the domain boundary
    elems.push({c, arc, ien, ring:B.ring, bEdge});
  });
  // boundary segments, one per outer element
  const bnd = [];
  elems.forEach((E,e) => { if (E.bEdge >= 0) bnd.push({e, local:E.bEdge, k:E.ring}); });
  bnd.sort((x,y) => x.k - y.k);
  return {nodes, elems, bnd, p, nen:(p+1)*(p+1)};
}

function buildID(){
  const pre = new Set();
  M.bnd.forEach(b => {
    if (!st.dir[b.k]) return;
    edgeLocal(b.local, M.p).forEach(A => pre.add(M.elems[b.e].ien[A]));
  });
  const ID = []; let eq = 0;
  for (let A=0;A<M.nodes.length;A++){
    if (pre.has(A)) ID.push(-1); else ID.push(eq++);
  }
  return {ID, neq:eq, pre};
}

/* ---------------- drawing ---------------- */
let TX = null;
function makeTx(){
  let lim = 1.0;
  M.nodes.forEach(n => { lim = Math.max(lim, Math.abs(n[0]), Math.abs(n[1])); });
  lim *= 1.04;
  const s = (VB - 2*PAD)/(2*lim);
  return {s, px: x => VB/2 + x*s, py: y => VB/2 - y*s,
             dx: q => (q - VB/2)/s, dy: q => -(q - VB/2)/s};
}
const esc = s => String(s);
const poly=(p,a)=>`<polygon points="${p.map(q=>q[0].toFixed(1)+','+q[1].toFixed(1)).join(' ')}" ${a}/>`;
const line=(a,b,c,d,s)=>`<line x1="${a.toFixed(1)}" y1="${b.toFixed(1)}" x2="${c.toFixed(1)}" y2="${d.toFixed(1)}" ${s}/>`;
const circ=(x,y,r,s)=>`<circle cx="${x.toFixed(1)}" cy="${y.toFixed(1)}" r="${r}" ${s}/>`;
const txt=(x,y,t,s)=>`<text x="${x.toFixed(1)}" y="${y.toFixed(1)}" ${s}>${esc(t)}</text>`;

function elemLoop(E, n){
  const pts = [];
  for (let i=0;i<4;i++)
    for (let j=0;j<n;j++) pts.push(edgePt(E.c, E.arc, i, j/n));
  return pts.map(q => [TX.px(q[0]), TX.py(q[1])]);
}

function hatch(E, local){
  const o = [], N = 13, L = 15;
  const pts = [];
  for (let j=0;j<=N;j++) pts.push(edgePt(E.c, E.arc, local, j/N));
  const px = pts.map(q => [TX.px(q[0]), TX.py(q[1])]);
  o.push(`<polyline points="${px.map(q=>q[0].toFixed(1)+','+q[1].toFixed(1)).join(' ')}" fill="none" stroke="${INK}" stroke-width="3"/>`);
  for (let j=0;j<N;j++){
    const a = px[j], b = px[j+1];
    let tx = b[0]-a[0], ty = b[1]-a[1];
    const len = Math.hypot(tx,ty) || 1; tx/=len; ty/=len;
    // outward normal: away from the centre of the picture
    let nx = ty, ny = -tx;
    const mx = (a[0]+b[0])/2 - VB/2, my = (a[1]+b[1])/2 - VB/2;
    if (nx*mx + ny*my < 0){ nx = -nx; ny = -ny; }
    const dx = (nx - tx)/Math.SQRT2, dy = (ny - ty)/Math.SQRT2;   // 45 degrees
    o.push(line(a[0], a[1], a[0]+L*dx, a[1]+L*dy, `stroke="${INK}" stroke-width="1.6"`));
  }
  return o.join("");
}

function render(){
  M = buildMesh(st.p);
  TX = makeTx();
  const {ID, neq, pre} = buildID();
  const p = M.p, nen = M.nen;
  $("dp_o").value = p; $("dsz_o").value = st.sz;

  // which elements are lit, and which local index to show at which node
  const lit = new Set(), locLab = new Map();      // global node -> [[e, A], ...]
  if (st.elem !== null) lit.add(st.elem);
  if (st.node !== null)
    M.elems.forEach((E,e) => { if (E.ien.includes(st.node)) lit.add(e); });
  M.elems.forEach((E,e) => {
    const show = $("t_allloc").checked || lit.has(e);
    if (!show) return;
    E.ien.forEach((g,A) => {
      if (st.node !== null && st.elem === null && g !== st.node && !$("t_allloc").checked) return;
      if (!locLab.has(g)) locLab.set(g, []);
      locLab.get(g).push([e, A]);
    });
  });

  const o = [];
  // element patches
  M.elems.forEach((E,e) => {
    const on = lit.has(e);
    o.push(poly(elemLoop(E, 22),
      `fill="${EC[e]}" fill-opacity="${on?1:0.55}" stroke="${on?ECs[e]:FAINT}" stroke-width="${on?2.6:1.4}" `+
      `data-elem="${e}" style="cursor:pointer"`));
  });
  // parametric grid lines inside each element, faint
  M.elems.forEach(E => {
    for (let k=1;k<p;k++){
      for (const fixed of [0,1]){
        const pts = [];
        for (let j=0;j<=16;j++){
          const t = j/16, u = fixed? k/p : t, v = fixed? t : k/p;
          const q = coons(E.c, E.arc, u, v); pts.push([TX.px(q[0]), TX.py(q[1])]);
        }
        o.push(`<polyline points="${pts.map(q=>q[0].toFixed(1)+','+q[1].toFixed(1)).join(' ')}" fill="none" stroke="${FAINT}" stroke-width="1"/>`);
      }
    }
  });
  // boundary: hatch the Dirichlet segments, plain line otherwise
  M.bnd.forEach(b => {
    const E = M.elems[b.e];
    if (st.dir[b.k]) o.push(hatch(E, b.local));
    else {
      const pts = [];
      for (let j=0;j<=22;j++) { const q = edgePt(E.c, E.arc, b.local, j/22); pts.push([TX.px(q[0]), TX.py(q[1])]); }
      o.push(`<polyline points="${pts.map(q=>q[0].toFixed(1)+','+q[1].toFixed(1)).join(' ')}" fill="none" stroke="${INK}" stroke-width="2.6"/>`);
    }
    // fat invisible hit strip
    const hp = [];
    for (let j=0;j<=22;j++) { const q = edgePt(E.c, E.arc, b.local, j/22); hp.push([TX.px(q[0]), TX.py(q[1])]); }
    o.push(`<polyline points="${hp.map(q=>q[0].toFixed(1)+','+q[1].toFixed(1)).join(' ')}" fill="none" stroke="transparent" stroke-width="18" data-bnd="${b.k}" style="cursor:pointer"/>`);
  });
  // element numbers
  // placed at v = 0.28 so it never lands on a node (nodes sit at v = k/p)
  if ($("t_elem").checked)
    M.elems.forEach((E,e) => {
      const q = coons(E.c, E.arc, 0.5, 0.28);
      o.push(txt(TX.px(q[0]), TX.py(q[1])+5, "e" + e,
        `text-anchor="middle" font-size="${st.sz+9}" font-weight="700" fill="${ECs[e]}" `+
        `opacity="0.75" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3.5" paint-order="stroke" style="pointer-events:none"`));
    });

  // nodes
  M.nodes.forEach((q,A) => {
    const X = TX.px(q[0]), Y = TX.py(q[1]);
    const sel = (A === st.node), isPre = pre.has(A);
    const r = sel ? 9 : 6;
    o.push(circ(X, Y, r+6, `fill="transparent" data-node="${A}" style="cursor:pointer"`));
    o.push(circ(X, Y, r, `fill="${sel?HOT:(isPre?PRE:"#fff")}" stroke="${INK}" stroke-width="${sel?2.4:1.5}" style="pointer-events:none"`));
    const gOn = $("t_glob").checked, iOn = $("t_id").checked;
    if (gOn || iOn){
      let inner = "";
      if (gOn) inner += `<tspan fill="${isPre?PRE:INK}" font-weight="600">${A}</tspan>`;
      if (gOn && iOn) inner += `<tspan fill="${GREY}">:</tspan>`;
      if (iOn) inner += `<tspan fill="${isPre?PRE:GREY}">${ID[A] < 0 ? "−1" : ID[A]}</tspan>`;
      o.push(`<text x="${X.toFixed(1)}" y="${(Y-r-4).toFixed(1)}" text-anchor="middle" `+
             `font-size="${st.sz}" font-family="monospace" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3" `+
             `paint-order="stroke" style="pointer-events:none">${inner}</text>`);
    }
    // local indices, offset per owning element so they do not collide
    const ls = locLab.get(A);
    if (ls) ls.forEach(([e,Aloc],i) => {
      const ang = -Math.PI/2 + (i+1)*(2*Math.PI/Math.max(3,ls.length+1));
      const rr = r + 13;
      o.push(txt(X + rr*Math.cos(ang), Y + rr*Math.sin(ang) + 3.5, Aloc,
        `text-anchor="middle" font-size="${st.sz}" font-weight="700" font-family="monospace" fill="${ECs[e]}" style="pointer-events:none"`));
    });
  });
  $("svg").innerHTML = o.join("");

  drawIEN(ID);
  drawIDs(ID, pre);
  readout(ID, neq, pre);
  $("idnote").textContent =
    `${M.nodes.length} global basis functions, ${neq} equations, ${M.nodes.length - neq} prescribed.`;
}

function drawIEN(ID){
  const p = M.p, nen = M.nen;
  let h = "<thead><tr><th>a</th>";
  for (let e=0;e<5;e++) h += `<th class="${st.elem===e?'col':''}" style="color:${ECs[e]}">e${e}</th>`;
  h += "</tr></thead><tbody>";
  for (let A=0;A<nen;A++){
    h += `<tr><th>${A}<span style="color:#9aa3ae;font-weight:400"> (${axi(A,p)},${aeta(A,p)})</span></th>`;
    for (let e=0;e<5;e++){
      const g = M.elems[e].ien[A];
      const cls = (st.node !== null && g === st.node) ? "hot" : (st.elem === e ? "col" : "");
      h += `<td class="${cls}" data-cell="${e},${A}" style="cursor:pointer">${g}</td>`;
    }
    h += "</tr>";
  }
  $("ient").innerHTML = h + "</tbody>";
}

function drawIDs(ID, pre){
  let h = "";
  for (let A=0;A<M.nodes.length;A++){
    const cls = (A === st.node ? "hot" : "") + (pre.has(A) ? " pre" : "");
    h += `<div class="${cls}" data-idn="${A}" style="cursor:pointer">${A}<span>${ID[A] < 0 ? "−1" : ID[A]}</span></div>`;
  }
  $("idt").innerHTML = h;
}

function readout(ID, neq, pre){
  const r = $("read");
  if (st.node !== null){
    const A = st.node, hits = [];
    M.elems.forEach((E,e) => E.ien.forEach((g,Al) => { if (g === A) hits.push([e,Al]); }));
    const where = hits.map(([e,Al]) =>
      `<span style="color:${ECs[e]}">IEN(${Al},&nbsp;${e})&nbsp;=&nbsp;${A}</span>`).join(" &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; ");
    r.innerHTML =
      `global basis function <b>A = ${A}</b> &nbsp; appears in ${hits.length} element${hits.length>1?"s":""}<br>` +
      where + `<br>` +
      (pre.has(A)
        ? `ID[${A}] = <b>−1</b> &nbsp; prescribed, so it contributes no equation; in assembly the <code>a</code> loop skips it and its known value moves to the right-hand side`
        : `ID[${A}] = <b>${ID[A]}</b> &nbsp; row and column ${ID[A]} of the global system`);
  } else if (st.elem !== null){
    const e = st.elem;
    r.innerHTML = `element <b>e${e}</b> &nbsp; local indices 0 … ${M.nen-1}, laid out by the stride rule `+
      `a = a<sub>ξ</sub> + (p+1)·a<sub>η</sub><br>` +
      `its ${M.nen} local basis functions map to global ` + M.elems[e].ien.join(", ");
  } else {
    r.innerHTML = `Click a node, an element, or a boundary edge.`;
  }
}

/* ---------------- interaction ---------------- */
$("svg").addEventListener("click", ev => {
  const t = ev.target;
  if (t.dataset.node !== undefined){ st.node = +t.dataset.node; st.elem = null; render(); return; }
  if (t.dataset.bnd  !== undefined){ const k = +t.dataset.bnd; st.dir[k] = !st.dir[k]; render(); return; }
  if (t.dataset.elem !== undefined){ st.elem = +t.dataset.elem; st.node = null; render(); return; }
});
$("ient").addEventListener("click", ev => {
  const c = ev.target.dataset.cell; if (!c) return;
  const [e,A] = c.split(",").map(Number);
  st.node = M.elems[e].ien[A]; st.elem = null; render();
});
$("idt").addEventListener("click", ev => {
  const n = ev.target.closest("[data-idn]"); if (!n) return;
  st.node = +n.dataset.idn; st.elem = null; render();
});
$("dp").addEventListener("input", e => { st.p = +e.target.value; st.node = null; st.elem = null; render(); });
$("dsz").addEventListener("input", e => { st.sz = +e.target.value; render(); });
for (const id of ["t_glob","t_id","t_allloc","t_elem"]) $(id).addEventListener("change", render);
$("b_alln").addEventListener("click", () => { st.dir = [false,false,false,false]; render(); });
$("b_alld").addEventListener("click", () => { st.dir = [true,true,true,true]; render(); });
$("b_clear").addEventListener("click", () => { st.node = null; st.elem = null; render(); });

st.dir = [true,false,false,false];
render();
})();
</script>
```

## What the widget is showing

**One global basis function, several local names.** Click any node on a shared edge. It
lights up in two elements, sometimes three or four at the inner corners, and the readout
lists every $\mathrm{IEN}(a,e)$ that returns it. That is the whole content of the IEN array:
the same unknown is local node 6 in one element and local node 2 in its neighbour, and
assembly has to add both contributions into the same global row.

**The local numbering is arbitrary, the global numbering is not.** Because the origins are
rotated, element 1's local node 0 is in a different physical corner from element 0's. The
mesh does not care. What matters is only that IEN is consistent with however each element
chose to number itself.

**Prescribed nodes drop out of the equations, not out of the mesh.** Hatch an edge and
watch the ID array: those nodes go to $-1$, and every ID value after them shifts down by
one, because equation numbers are consecutive over the *unknowns*. The node is still there,
still has a basis function, still appears in IEN. It just has no equation of its own, and
its known value moves to the right-hand side of its neighbours' equations.

**Two different lengths.** IEN is indexed by local node and element, so it has
$n_{en} \times n_{el}$ entries no matter what the boundary conditions are. ID is indexed by
global node, so it has $n_{bf}$ entries, of which $n_{eq}$ are equation numbers. Changing a
boundary condition changes ID and leaves IEN untouched.

## Things to try

1. Click the node at the centre of a shared edge between two outer elements. It has two
   local names. Now click an inner corner of the middle element: three elements meet there,
   so it has three.
2. Hatch one edge, then a second. Watch $n_{eq}$ drop and the equation numbers renumber.
   The corner shared by the two hatched edges is prescribed once, not twice.
3. Set all four edges to Dirichlet. Every boundary node goes to $-1$ and only the interior
   nodes carry equations — at degree 1 that leaves just the four inner corners.
4. Set every edge to Neumann. Nothing is prescribed, $n_{eq} = n_{bf}$, and the global
   matrix would be singular: this is the two-prescribed-fluxes case from Project 1, Task 5,
   in two dimensions.
5. Change the degree from 2 to 1. The disk becomes a square and the mid-edge nodes
   disappear, but the five elements and their connectivity are unchanged — degree changes
   the number of basis functions, not the mesh.
6. Go to degree 3 and turn on **all local indices**. This is what the bookkeeping actually
   looks like at modest degree, and why nobody writes it out by hand.
